question: How many human-written demonstration prompts were used for supervised fine-tuning of Llama 2-Chat?
answer: According to [Source 1], **27,540 high-quality human-written demonstration prompts** were used for supervised fine-tuning of Llama 2-Chat.
context:
[Source 1] Llama 2: Open Foundation and Fine-Tuned Chat Models from Meta AI
Llama 2, released by Meta AI in July 2023, presents a family of open-weight large language models trained from scratch on 2 trillion tokens of publicly available data. The model family includes 7B, 13B, 34B, and 70B parameter sizes. Improvements over Llama 1 include a 40% larger pretraining corpus, doubled context window (4096 vs. 2048 tokens), grouped-query attention (GQA) for the 34B and 70B models for efficient inference, and better training stability. The pretraining data mix includes CommonCrawl, C4, GitHub, Wikipedia, books, ArXiv papers, and StackExchange, with upsampled high-quality sources.

The instruction-tuned variants (Llama 2-Chat) use supervised fine-tuning (SFT) on 27,540 high-quality human-written demonstration prompts, followed by RLHF with PPO using two reward models trained on over 1 million pairwise comparisons. A novel Ghost Attention (GAtt) mechanism maintains instruction consistency across long multi-turn conversations. Llama 2 70B achieves 68.9% on MMLU (5-shot), 85.1% on HellaSwag, and 35.4% on HumanEval. Safety evaluations show that Llama 2-Chat models exhibit significantly lower rates of harmful responses than Llama 1 (0.7% vs. 15.3% violation rate on Anthropic's red-teaming dataset).

Llama 2's open release under a commercial-friendly license catalyzed an explosion of open-source LLM development. Derivative models including Code Llama (code-specialized, 7B-34B with 100K context), WizardLM-2, and Orca 2 proliferated rapidly. The architecture—RoPE positional embeddings, SwiGLU activation, RMSNorm—became the de facto standard for subsequent open models. Mistral 7B used the same architecture with sliding window attention, outperforming Llama 2 13B while being smaller. Llama 3 (Meta, April 2024) extended the series to 8B and 70B models trained on 15 trillion tokens with a 128K vocabulary tokenizer, achieving 82.0% on MMLU and setting new open-source performance standards across reasoning, coding, and multilingual tasks.

---

[Source 2] Rotary Position Embeddings (RoPE) and Long Context Extension in LLMs
The base frequency θ=10000 limits effective context to roughly 2-4x the training length. Llama 3 increases the base frequency to θ=500000 to support longer sequences before interpolation degrades. Practical long-context applications enabled by RoPE extensions include retrieval-augmented generation over long documents, multi-document reasoning, repository-level code generation, and long-form creative writing. Code Llama achieves 100K context via RoPE scaling, enabling retrieval over entire codebases. Mistral uses sliding window attention (SWA) with a window size of 4096 tokens and rolling buffer cache to achieve effective 32K context without full quadratic attention cost. The combination of FlashAttention-2 and extended RoPE has made 128K+ context windows practical in both training and inference for production LLM applications.

---

[Source 3] Prompt Engineering Techniques and Best Practices for LLMs
mat explicitly (JSON schema, bullet points, length constraints); (4) For complex tasks, break into subtasks rather than asking for everything at once; (5) For reasoning tasks, always request explanation before conclusion; (6) Use system prompts for persistent instructions and user prompts for per-request context; (7) Temperature=0 for factual extraction, temperature=0.7-1.0 for creative tasks. Prompt injection attacks—where adversarial text in user input or retrieved context overrides the system prompt—represent an active security concern for production LLM applications, with countermeasures including instruction hierarchy enforcement and sandboxed tool execution.
